title: The Holy Innocents (28 December)
hookLine: Herod's massacre remembered; a day for all children who suffer

lines: THE SCENE THE CRIBS LEAVE OUT.
cards: There's a carol from Coventry, in England, that sounds like a lullaby, soft and slow, sung by mothers to their babies. Then you listen to the words, and you realize the mothers are singing because soldiers are coming.
It's from a medieval play about this day. Three days after Christmas, the Church remembers the darkest scene in the infancy story, one that nativity sets leave out.
It belongs to the season anyway: Matthew tells it in the same chapter as the star.

teach.h: THE MAGI GO HOME ANOTHER WAY.
teach.b: In Matthew's gospel, the magi stop in Jerusalem asking where the newborn king of the Jews is. King Herod, who has a long record of killing anyone he sees as a rival, asks them to report back.
They don't; they go home another way.
Joseph, warned in a dream, takes Mary and the child by night and flees to Egypt. And Herod, furious, sends soldiers to kill every boy in Bethlehem and its borders two years old and under.
Matthew reaches back to the prophet Jeremiah. In the Douay-Rheims: "Rachel bewailing her children, and would not be comforted, because they are not."
Rachel, the wife of Jacob, was buried by tradition on the road near Bethlehem.
Jeremiah pictured her weeping over her people carried into exile; Matthew hears her weeping again.

teach.h: NO OTHER SOURCE, AND A SMALL TOWN.
teach.b: An honest note: no other ancient source records this massacre. The historian Josephus describes Herod's cruelty at length, including the killing of his own sons, but not this.
Bethlehem was a small village, and many scholars think the number of children would have been small too, perhaps a dozen or two, though later legends grew it into thousands.
The Church honors these children as martyrs, not because they chose to die for Christ, but because they died in his place, too young to say a word.
So the day has become a day for every child who suffers from the violence of the powerful: in war, in hunger, in flight, in danger at home. The Holy Family themselves end this story as refugees.

how: Catholics keep December 28 as the feast of the Holy Innocents, and many parishes and families use it to pray for children who suffer, including the unborn, refugees and children in war.

games.q: you're Joseph. you've just woken from a dream: take the child and his mother and flee. it's the middle of the night. what do you do?
o: wait until morning and ask the priests.
get up and go to Egypt that night.
games.why: Matthew says he arose and took the child and his mother by night and went into Egypt. the family becomes refugees.

practice: Bring to mind children who are not safe tonight: in a war zone you've seen on the news, in a shelter, in a hospital, in a hard home down the street.

Don't look away, and don't try to fix it in two minutes; just let them be real to you, one at a time. If you pray, pray for them by name or by place; if not, let your attention be a kind of keeping watch.

wordCard.voice: Herod, the king. Matthew's gospel: in his fury at the magi's escape, he sent soldiers to kill the children of Bethlehem, honored on December 28. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: Rachel weeping for her children, Jeremiah 31:15 (31:14 in Hebrew Bibles).

carryVoice: Your line: rachel weeping. Her grief is allowed to stay grief, for today at least. Until tomorrow.
